submission.justification: Module-D3 at 30% coverage gave the highest simulated light collection: 52.5 PE/MeV, against 36.2 for D1 at the same coverage. The 2025 summary has D3 ahead of D1 and D2 at 20% coverage too. The meeting notes confirm enough feedthroughs for 30% coverage, and the cold amplifiers are validated for every design. Caveat: no document or simulation addresses robustness. D3 uses a thin bonded dichroic filter, and its bond could fail under cryogenic cycling. The modules cannot be reached once the cryostat is filled, so this should be checked with cryogenic thermal-cycling and bond-integrity tests before the Q3 design freeze. I did not simulate D2, because the 2025 results had it lowest at 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage.

requirements.evidence: D3 at 30% coverage gave 52.5 PE/MeV. D1 at 30% gave 36.2. In the 2025 results at 20% coverage, D3 was 38, D1 27 and D2 18.

requirements.requirement: Module is one of the three listed designs

requirements.evidence: No document gives robustness or cryogenic reliability data. D3's thin bonded dichroic filter is a possible delamination risk. Cryogenic validation is needed.
30% is within range, and the feedthroughs support it.
